nodes.summary: The depth of an index $(k_1, \ldots, k_r)$ is its number of entries $r$.
nodes.title: Depth of an index

nodes.summary: The entries of an index $(k_1, \ldots, k_r)$ form the list $[k_1, \ldots, k_r]$ of its terms, in order.
nodes.title: Entries of an index

nodes.summary: The height of an index $(k_1, \ldots, k_r)$ is the number of positions $i$ with $1 \le i \le r$ and $k_i \ge 2$.
nodes.title: Height of an index

nodes.summary: For a positive integer $k$, the Hoffman block $z_k = x^{k-1} y$ is the word in the free monoid on two letters $x$ and $y$ consisting of $k - 1$ copies of $x$ followed by one $y$.
nodes.title: Hoffman block

nodes.summary: An index is a finite sequence $(k_1, \ldots, k_r)$ of positive integers with $r \ge 0$, so the empty sequence is allowed. It is represented as a natural number $n$ together with a composition of $n$, that is, a sequence of positive integers with sum $n$.
nodes.title: Multiple-zeta index

nodes.summary: A list $[k_1, \ldots, k_r]$ of natural numbers is admissible when it is nonempty ($r \ge 1$), $k_1 \ge 2$, and $k_i > 0$ for every $i$ with $2 \le i \le r$.
nodes.title: Admissible list

nodes.summary: An index is admissible if and only if the list of its entries is an admissible list.
nodes.title: Admissibility of an index via its entries

nodes.summary: An index $(k_1, \ldots, k_r)$ is admissible when it is nonempty ($r \ge 1$) and its first entry satisfies $k_1 \ge 2$.
nodes.title: Admissible index

nodes.summary: For every positive integer $k$, the list of letters of the Hoffman block $z_k$ consists of $k - 1$ copies of $x$ (false) followed by one $y$ (true).
nodes.title: Hoffman block as a list

nodes.summary: The weight of an index $(k_1, \ldots, k_r)$ is the sum $k_1 + \cdots + k_r$ of its entries.
nodes.title: Weight of an index

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
